traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Guttiferae incl. Hypericaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina undivided, margins entire.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Guttiferae (incl. Hypericaceae, read 2026-10-16): leaves mostly opposite; family states opposite usually, so crossing pairs.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312: 4 to 5 sepals and petals.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312: ovary of 3 to 5 carpels.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312: 4 to 5 free, often contorted petals. Free petals: rotate by PlantGen's free-petal rule; the book names no other corolla form.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 312, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 158 Hypericaceae: trees to herbs, rarely climbers, with resinous sap; leaves opposite or whorled, simple, often dotted with glands; no stipules; flowers showy, yellow or white, regular, mostly at the shoot tips, alone to in cymose panicles; stamens numerous, often in bundles; ovary of one or 3 to 5 cells, superior (the stamens below it); fruit a capsule or berry, rarely a drupe. The stamens' 10 to 200 reads 'numerous', inferred.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 309, 311, 312, family Hypericaceae: leaf margin entire; read as "entire".

traits.inflorescence.note: Wikipedia Hypericum (read 2026-10-17): c. 490-518 species, the great majority of Hypericaceae (~600-700 spp). NZ Flora genus factsheet for Hypericum (read 2026-10-17): inflorescences terminal, in cymes or panicles. The family file's earlier DELTA Guttiferae reading also says terminal and cymose. So cyme leads; corymbiform cymes (many Hypericum, Vismia, Harungana) and single flowers (small-flowered and shrubby Hypericum) stay often. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 309, 311, 312, family Hypericaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".
